prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor room under renovation across five frames as the camera wearer turns clockwise from a close white wall corner (frames 1–2, roughly 0.3–1.0 m away) past an upper wall/ceiling expanse and window recess (frame 3, 0.5–2.5 m) toward an A-frame ladder and open room floor below (frames 4–5). In frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, the wearer's own right arm, flashlight, and the left ladder rails appear brightest in the foreground within arm's reach (0.2–0.6 m), while a second person standing on the floor behind and to the right of the ladder in frames 4–5 is rendered in mid-to-dark grey at roughly 2.0–2.5 m from the wearer and 1.0–1.5 m beyond the ladder. In frame 4, the ladder rungs and rails clearly occlude the standing person, who faces and looks upward toward the camera wearer while extending their right hand forward within reach of the ladder's back side in frame 5, with a miter saw stand and windows situated another 1.5–2.5 m behind and to the right of that person. The depth map makes the continuous 3D surface gradients of the featureless white walls and the exact foreground-background separation between the ladder rungs and the occluded person much easier to see than in the brightly lit RGB frames alone. However, the map is unreliable across the glass window panes (which blend smoothly with surrounding frames rather than showing outdoor depth), in the far background of frames 4–5 where the person's head and the room beyond ~3 m collapse into uniform black, and in frame 1 where the top-right wall is over-saturated as closer than the floor corner.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates body regions in the scene against a black background as the camera wearer rotates from facing a close corner on the left (frames 1–2) toward an elevated view looking down and right at a standing person behind a ladder (frames 4–5). It detects the camera wearer's own lower torso/left arm at the bottom of frame 1, right forearm holding a flashlight at the right edge of frame 2, and raised right hand/arm in the lower-right foreground of frames 4–5 (all within 0.2–0.6 m, partly cropped by the lower frame borders). In frame 4, the second person standing ~2.0–2.5 m away behind the ladder is split by the occluding ladder rungs into two separate 'person' masks (head above and torso/legs below), whereas in frame 5—after the wearer turns right to clear the ladder occlusion—the standing person appears as a tall pink mask facing and looking up toward the wearer with an adjacent light-blue 'person' mask on a background figure or object directly behind their left shoulder (~2.5–3.0 m away, 0.3–0.5 m behind them). While segmentation clearly delineates the occluded body fragments between the ladder rungs in frame 4 and separates the wearer's foreground arm from the cluttered tool background in frame 5, it fails to segment any structural objects like the ladder, windows, flashlight, or miter saw. It is also highly unreliable in frame 3, where it misclassifies the entire featureless white wall and ceiling plane (0.5–2.0 m in front of and above the wearer) as a massive 'bed' mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1–3 when only the camera wearer's heavily cropped limbs and walls are in view, and activates only in frames 4–5 as the wearer turns toward the ladder and the wider room to the right. In frame 4, it detects only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand holding a flashlight in the lower-right foreground (~0.3–0.4 m away, within immediate arm's reach), completely missing the second person standing ~2.0–2.5 m away behind the occluding ladder rungs. In frame 5, as the camera turns further right and the ladder moves to the left edge, the map captures a yellow body skeleton and a magenta hand skeleton for the standing person (~2.0 m in front of and below the wearer), showing their torso angled toward the wearer, head tilted up looking at the camera, left arm hanging down by their left hip, and right arm extended forward toward the ladder and camera wearer. This skeletal representation makes the exact joint articulation and upward-facing orientation of the standing person in frame 5 and the finger curl of the wearer's gripping hand in frame 4 immediately explicit despite harsh flashlight glare and background clutter in the RGB image. However, the pose estimator is unreliable whenever bodies are partly out of view or occluded, failing to track the wearer's own extended arm in frames 1, 2, and 5, missing the occluded person entirely in frame 4, and misplacing the standing person's right wrist and magenta hand cluster in frame 5 onto a white object to their left rather than their actual outstretched right hand.
